rationale.conceptual: The core method is a routine application of DFT with a standard functional (GGA-PW91), using plane-wave pseudopotentials. The analysis steps (EOS fitting, common tangent, enthalpy equality, elastic constants, mechanical stability criterion, quasi-harmonic Debye model) are well-documented and not novel. The reproduction task requires standard implementation choices, not new derivation or custom algorithm design.
rationale.execution: The pipeline spans ~6 stages (DFT energy-volume scans, EOS fitting, elastic constant calculations under pressure, stability analysis, Debye model runs, and final curve extraction) with dependencies among them. While each stage uses established codes, orchestrating the workflow (preparing inputs, running multiple DFT jobs, collecting outputs, and post-processing) constitutes a non-trivial multi-step engineering task, fitting the description of a 4-6 stage pipeline.

difficulty.reasoning: This is a standard DFT study applying established methods (GGA-PW91, EOS fitting, elastic constants, Debye model) to a simple material (SiC). The method is routine for computational condensed matter physics and does not require novel algorithm development. The pipeline involves several sequential steps (DFT runs, EOS fitting, elastic constants, Debye model) but the tooling is well-known (Quantum ESPRESSO, Gibbs2) and the workflow is linear. Computational demands are modest for modern hardware – small unit cells and moderate k-point sampling run on a few CPU cores with a few GB of RAM, and no GPU is required. The discipline is computational materials science.

compute_estimate.reasoning: The paper uses primitive unit cells (2 atoms) with a moderate 550 eV cutoff and a 12x12x12 k-mesh. Total energy and elastic constant calculations for ~20-30 configurations are feasible on a few CPU cores. Memory footprint is small; a few GB of RAM suffice. No GPU is needed, and input data are trivial (pseudopotential files and initial structures).
